step_by_step_reasoning:
The architecture illustrates a migration and ELT data pipeline from on-premises databases to Amazon Redshift for a life sciences client.
1. **Data Ingestion (Flow 0):** On-premises databases transfer daily incremental data (around 100 GB/day) through an AWS Storage Gateway over an NFS interface. The data is transported across AWS Direct Connect (2x 10G links) into a Landing S3 bucket.
2. **ELT Processing (Flow 1):** From the Landing S3 bucket, EC2 instances run Quality Cleansing scripts controlled by metadata and pipeline scripts stored in an RDS Postgres database. Cleansed data is written to a Transformation S3 bucket. Subsequent Transformation EC2 nodes execute script logic driven by RDS metadata to format facts and dimensions, loading them directly into Amazon Redshift.
3. **Publishing & Archival (Flow 2):** Redshift Spectrum exports processed data to a Publish S3 bucket for daily dashboard reporting. S3 lifecycle policies automatically transition data from the Publish bucket to S3 Glacier for long-term archiving after 1 year and 1 month.

graph.name: Capgemini Life Sciences Netezza to Redshift Data Migration & Processing Architecture
graph.notes: This HIPAA-compliant architecture ingests 100 GB daily increments over a 2x 10G Direct Connect link. It replaces a legacy Netezza data warehouse with Amazon Redshift using an ELT model driven by RDS Postgres metadata.

nodes.name: On-Prem Database
nodes.notes: Hosts historical database source systems (~20 TB total).

nodes.name: Storage Gateway
nodes.notes: AWS Storage Gateway deployed on-premises using NFS volumes to ingest daily database increments (100 GB/day).

nodes.name: Direct Connect
nodes.notes: Dual 10G AWS Direct Connect aggregated links with SSL encryption.

nodes.name: Landing S3
nodes.notes: Landing zone S3 bucket with 2-day retention period (1 active + 1 buffer day).

nodes.name: Quality Cleansing
nodes.notes: EC2 compute instances executing data quality and cleansing checks.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: PostgreSQL RDS storing all ELT metadata, pipeline controls, and transformation scripts.

nodes.name: Transformation S3
nodes.notes: Transformation zone S3 bucket with a 1-day retention period.

nodes.name: Transformation
nodes.notes: EC2 compute instances transforming cleansed data into facts and dimensions.

nodes.name: RedShift
nodes.notes: Amazon Redshift cluster storing dimensional model data, queried via Redshift Spectrum.

nodes.name: Publish S3
nodes.notes: Publish zone S3 bucket feeding daily reporting dashboards with a retention of 1 year and 1 month.

nodes.name: Glacier
nodes.notes: S3 Glacier archive for long-term retention of historical data.

edges.notes: On-prem database ingests daily changes into Storage Gateway via NFS volumes.
Storage Gateway streams data over Direct Connect connection.
Direct Connect delivers ingested datasets to the Landing S3 bucket.
Quality Cleansing EC2 nodes pull raw files from Landing S3.
RDS supplies metadata and cleansing scripts to Quality Cleansing EC2 instances.
Quality Cleansing EC2 writes cleansed data into Transformation S3.
Transformation EC2 instances pull cleansed data from Transformation S3.
RDS provides metadata and ELT transformation logic to Transformation EC2 instances.
Transformation EC2 loads transformed facts and dimension tables into Redshift.
Redshift Spectrum publishes daily aggregated reporting datasets to Publish S3 bucket.
Lifecycle rule transitions data from Publish S3 to S3 Glacier after 1 year and 1 month.
